sources_considered.why: Cursor’s explanation identifies tokens per request as a cost driver. It does not disclose its AWS bills or supplier contracts.
The contemporaneous launch announcement states that headline token prices were unchanged. This does not settle effective caching or contractual charges.
The targeted read found no May 30, 2025 entry establishing the claimed service-tier change.
Read to identify the proposed service-tier and caching mechanism, not as independent proof of billing or causation.

evidence_items.locator: Section “Why did we change the plan?”

receipt.public_excerpt: New models can spend more tokens per request on longer-horizon tasks.

evidence_items.explanation: Cursor identifies a usage-intensity mechanism for higher costs. This is a material alternative explanation, but it neither quantifies the AWS increase nor excludes a simultaneous price effect.

evidence_items.locator: Opening section, paragraph describing model availability and pricing

receipt.public_excerpt: Pricing remains consistent with previous Opus and Sonnet models

evidence_items.explanation: Unchanged headline token prices limit a simple across-the-board price-rise explanation. They do not establish Cursor’s effective prices, caching mix, or service-tier commitments.

unresolved_gaps: No independent confirmation of the two Cursor AWS cash-payment totals was found.
Cursor’s effective Anthropic contracts, discounts, and service-tier commitments were not available.
No decomposition separates price effects from usage, model mix, caching, other services, or payment timing.
